title: COVID-19 Vaccination Responses with Different Vaccine Platforms in Patients with Inborn Errors of Immunity.
ehr_evidence: The study prospectively collected blood/plasma/serum and PBMC samples from patients and healthy controls, analyzed by ELISA, pseudovirus neutralization assay, ELISPOT, and flow cytometry; no electronic health record or administrative database was used.
summary: A prospective observational cohort study evaluating the safety and immunogenicity (humoral and cellular immune responses) of five COVID-19 vaccine platforms in 118 adult and pediatric patients with inborn errors of immunity compared with 37 age-matched healthy controls in Argentina.
key_findings: Anti-S/RBD IgG titers were significantly lower in IEI patients than in age-matched healthy controls (p < 0.05 for both pediatric and adult cohorts).
Neutralizing antibody titers (IC80) were significantly lower in IEI patients than in healthy controls (pediatric p < 0.01, adult p < 0.05).
Positive S-specific IFN-γ cellular response was observed in 84.5% of IEI patients.
82.1% of IEI patients presented S-specific circulating T follicular-helper (TFH) cells.
Circulating TFH cell frequency was significantly lower in IEI patients than in healthy controls (3.1% vs 8.9%, p < 0.0001).
Neutralizing capacity was significantly higher in pediatric than adult IEI patients (p < 0.001).
Moderna vaccine elicited a stronger humoral response than other platforms (antibody titer p < 0.01 and neutralization p < 0.005), while cellular (IFN-γ) response did not differ by vaccine platform.
No significant difference in humoral response was observed between vaccinated patients with or without previous SARS-CoV-2 infection.
No moderate or severe vaccine-associated adverse events were observed.
captured_features: Neutralizing antibody titers (IC80/IC50) by pseudovirus assay
Circulating TFH cell frequency by flow cytometry (CD4+CXCR5+PD-1+CD154+)
pathologies_diseases: Inborn errors of immunity (IEI; e.g., CVID, XLA, specific antibody deficiency, selective IgA deficiency, hypogammaglobulinemia, hyper IgM syndrome, combined immunodeficiencies)
study_design: Prospective observational cohort study with age-matched healthy controls
population: 118 adults and pediatric patients with inborn errors of immunity (aged 12-78 years) and 37 age-matched healthy controls (27 adults, 12 adolescents) in Argentina
exposure_domain: COVID-19 vaccination (vaccine platforms: mRNA, adenoviral vector, inactivated, and combinations)
limitations: Observational design with a relatively small sample size and heterogeneous IEI subtypes
No long-term follow-up, so long-term humoral and cellular immunogenicity remains unknown
Healthy controls were recruited from healthcare workers and children of healthcare workers, not population-based
data_availability_statement: All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this published article (and its supplementary information files).
